column3: Close to the Hebrew; “mountain goats of the rock” is rendered “wild mountain goats,” and אַיָּלוֹת (“does”) “the deer.”
Close to the Hebrew; בַבָּר (“in the open field”) is rendered “with grain.”
Close to the Hebrew; עָרוֹד (“the wild ass”) is rendered “the onager.”
Close to the Hebrew; מְלֵחָה (“salt land”) is rendered “the barren land.”
The verse is difficult; NKJV renders “wave proudly” and takes חֲסִידָה as “the kindly stork,” forming a question.
Close to the Hebrew; “without fear” is rendered “without concern.”
NKJV renders רַעְמָה (“a mane”) as “thunder,” following an older understanding of the word.
Close to the Hebrew; “make it leap like the locust” is rendered “frighten him like a locust.”
Close to the Hebrew; “to meet the weapons” is rendered “into the clash of arms.”
Close to the Hebrew; “swallows the ground” is rendered “devours the distance.”
Close to the Hebrew; נֵץ (“a falcon”) is rendered “the hawk.”
Close to the Hebrew; “at your mouth” is rendered “at your command.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the tooth of the rock” is rendered “the crag of the rock.”
